Working entry (`chk-nfpsqhbe`): «Canvas draw commands — a driver verb answering a canvas's commands, summary and full
levels, deterministic, diffable; size measured; every carrier's crossing the founder's fork (v040-10)». Epoch 4 —
Inside the canvas, its second entry (the first, «Upstream sync ahead of inside the canvas», is wrapped).

- A read of a canvas's content as data: the draw commands an app's `Widget::paint` records into its anyrender
  `Scene` (fill, stroke, glyph run, push layer, push clip layer, push mask layer, pop layer, box shadow), read for one
  canvas element named by its stable element id, on the held instance, running no step and changing nothing.

- Two levels: a summary level (a count per command kind and the canvas's size, or a like closed digest of the scene)
  and a full level (one line or object per command in paint order, layers as nesting — the Flutter display-list form
  the research leans on, `escher-0.4.0-incubator/canvas-research-2026-11-18.md` §3 and §5 item 3).

- Deterministic and independent of hardware: two reads of one state answer the same bytes, in process and across
  processes, and on CI's linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 hosts; numbers written at a stated rounding.

- Diffable: two reads of one canvas before and after a step compare to name exactly what changed (the dump's lines
  added, removed or changed), and a step that changes nothing reads an empty diff.

- Size measured: the dump of Circle Drawer's canvas on the stand, at each level, at boot and after circles are
  added, stated in bytes against the snapshot's 10,000-byte budget.

Given by one question dialog of three in overseer1's session on the evening of 2026-11-24, each question put whole
with every option and its cost and the probe's numbers, and told «every arm but the first reverses your "pixels alone"
of 2026-11-23»; relayed verbatim by overseer1 to the escher overseer (received 2026-11-24T17:01Z) and by the escher

file's own option letter.

His answer: «Глагол canvas на всех каналах (Recommended)»

The forks file's option **F1 B**: a sixteenth verb, `canvas`, on every ratified carrier — the session socket, the
command line, MCP and a kept check; to the model provider only through MCP. His own word reverses «canvas content
crosses as pixels alone» for this verb on those carriers.

## F3 — «Что выходит наружу из ТЕКСТА…?»
His answer: «Без текста, только сводка (Recommended)»

The forks file's option **F3 A**: no text in any form — per glyph run its glyph count, font size, bounding box, brush
and a 64-bit digest of its glyph ids; closed values and a digest only.

## F5 — «Где новый глагол canvas проверяется…?»
His answer: «Тестовый canvas (Recommended)»

The forks file's option **F5 B**: the carriers are proven on a test-only canvas fixture served by a test host. Circle
Drawer stays in process; his «A: не сейчас» of 2026-11-23 stands.

    - **Deterministic.** Two reads of one state answer the same bytes. A committed `TABLE` holds each answer's
      `answer_digest` and its byte count, its row count asserted (tests S4):
      - at boot, after the click, at 12 circles and at 100 circles;
      - the summary, the whole full dump and every part.
      - The 12- and 100-circle states are written to `data-circles` through the held harness's mutator from the
        probe's fixed sequence, then settled.
      - One value per state, level and part, both modes reading it.
      - The windows and macOS legs read the same table (test-plan · decision/stand-checks-in-both-layout-modes;
        architecture · decision/stand-readings-same-on-every-ci-os).
    - **Size measured.** The sizes are re-measured with the `pop` lines and the written fields the probe did not
      write. Predicted near the probe's (about 450 B a circle; 12 circles whole within the budget; 100 circles in
      parts) — record what the run measures and pin it.
      - `a_full_dump_over_the_budget_reads_in_parts_each_within_it`:
        - every part of the 100-circle dump is within 10,000 bytes;
        - the parts' `text` in order is the whole dump's `text` as `json` writes it unpaged;
        - `fonts` stands in part 1 alone;
        - a part past the last is empty.
    - **Changes nothing.** `a_canvas_read_changes_nothing_with_timer_ticks_pending`: a `canvas` call leaves the
      snapshot, both focus readings, the next diff and the clock unchanged, under a control with pending work
      (test-plan · decision/no-change-read-control-needs-pending-work).
      - On the Timer with delivered ticks unapplied, `canvas` on `timer-elapsed` answers `canvas: false` and the ticks
        stay unapplied.
      - On Circle Drawer the summary and the dump read the same before and after.
    - **Refusals.**
      - An unread id is refused `not-found`; a deleted CRUD row's id `stale`. Nothing changes.
      - A document whose font context resolves no `sans-serif` family is refused `fonts-unavailable`, and the
        `actions` read names the same cause for `canvas` there (test-plan · decision/shot-refused-without-fonts, the
        fixture `stand_act_screenshot` reads).

11. **The test-only canvas fixture** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs`).
    - Add one shared fixture page `canvas_commands()`. Two checks read it: step 12's file and `stand_mcp_tools`
      (test-plan · decision/shared-fixture-pages).
    - It holds two keyed `object` canvases:
      - `small-canvas` — a widget painting a clip layer, a solid fill, a stroked circle and the glyphs of the text
        `QZX` shaped from the document's own font context (`Widget::fonts`), then the pop;
      - `large-canvas` — 200 solid fills, so its full dump passes the budget.
    - It also holds a keyed `button`.
    - No print, tracing call, env read, file or net (test-plan · decision/shared-fixtures-in-one-module).

12. **Every carrier, on the fixture** (new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_carriers.rs`). Both layout modes;
    every wait bounded; a failure names a mode, a carrier and an index (tests S4, S6).
    - **The socket** (`cfg(unix)`, item by item: test-plan · decision/socket-session-checks-unix-gated).
      - Two `#[ignore]` host tests serve `fixtures::hold` of the fixture through `escher_driver::serve`, spawned as
        children of the test binary by `session_common::host_command` and held behind `Host`, as
        `stand_act_error_text` does (:878–900).
      - Through `escher_driver::call`, each of these answers the line `to_json` writes for the same call on a fresh
        in-process session:
        - `canvas` on `small-canvas` with no flag, with `full`, and with `part` 1;
        - on `large-canvas` with `full`, then parts 1 and 2;
        - on the button.
      - The host is stopped and its state directory removed.
    - **MCP,** in process through `session_common::serve_lines`, the boot closure booting the fixture under its label.
      - The same calls as `tools/call` answer one text block, decoded whole through the shared helper (test-plan ·
        decision/mcp-result-decoded-whole), equal to the in-process line.
      - A call with no `id` is one text block with `isError` true.
    - **A kept check** (`cfg(unix)`).
      - `session_common::record_check` keeps the three `small-canvas` calls and a `large-canvas` part.
        `Check::from_bytes` reads it.
      - `Check::replay` on a fresh session replays it green.
      - Its kept `digest` field flipped stops the replay at that step naming `digest` (test-plan ·
        contract/check-replay/stop).
    - **F3 A and F4 A hold on every carrier:** `the_fixtures_answers_hold_no_glyph_id_and_no_text`.
      - The full dump's glyph line holds exactly the keys `font size brush t n at ids`, `n=3` and an `ids` value of 16
        lowercase hex.
      - No answer, MCP result or kept check byte holds `QZX` or `DejaVu`.

13. **The command line through the binary, on a canvas** (`examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs`, already
    `cfg(unix)`; test-plan · decision/cli-checks-through-own-binary).
    - The file states its own small canvas page: a keyed canvas `seven-canvas` with a clip, a fill, a stroke and a
      glyph run from the document's fonts. It is a page with one reader in another crate (test-plan ·
      decision/shared-fixture-pages, its except).
    - An `#[ignore]` host test serves it through `escher_driver::serve`. The check spawns it from its own test binary
      and runs the package's `escher-session` binary against that state directory:
      - `canvas --id seven-canvas` exits 0 with the summary's keys;
      - `--full` exits 0 with `canvas text fonts images`;
      - `--full --part 1` exits 0 with `part` and `parts`;
      - with no `--id` it is refused `malformed`, status 1 (design-system ·
        contract/escher-session-commands/layout-arguments, its form).
    - On the served Counter, `canvas --id counter-increment` answers `canvas: false`.
    - The module doc (:2) reads «each of the twelve verbs».
    - Stdout is one uncoloured line with no ESC byte (design-system · decision/escher-session-no-colour), and stderr
      is empty with `RUST_LOG` unset (obs S1).

14. **The stand's other readers** (blitz-tests).
    - `session_common/mod.rs`:
      - gains `canvas(id)`, `canvas_full(id)` and `canvas_part(id, n)` call builders and a `canvased(session, call)`
        reader;
      - takes the three outcomes among the non-acting outcomes (:245).
    - `stand_actions.rs`:
      - every listed node carries six target verbs, `canvas` last with no cause (`nodes.len() * 6` at :262 and :501);
      - its every-cause-is-the-call's check covers `canvas`;
      - the Cells bound test (:566) re-reads the answer's size. Predicted: it grows by about 17 bytes per listed node
        and stays within 1,048,576 — record the measured size; the bound does not move (security-plan ·
        decision/actions-answer-unpaged).
    - `stand_cross_os_readings.rs`: re-read the `actions` rows of `TABLE` (:24), seven tasks at two moments, on linux
      in both modes.
      - Predicted: the 14 `actions` rows move and the 40 snapshot and lint rows do not — record what the re-run
        measures.
      - A snapshot or lint row that moves is this chunk's defect, never re-pinned.
    - `stand_act_spans.rs`:
      - one `canvas` call per mode accepted, recording `verb` alone, and one refused (no id), recording `verb` and
        `cause`;
      - the calls-per-mode count moves by two;
      - the module doc (:3) and the message at :536 read «twelve verbs».
    - `stand_mcp_tools.rs`: `a_canvas_tool_call_answers_the_runs_line_and_parents_a_command_recording_its_verb_alone` on
      the fixture. Its result text is the in-process line, and its `tool_call` parents one `command` child (obs-plan ·
      contract/tool-call-span/command-child).
    - `stand_replay.rs`: no change; the fixture's replay is step 12's.
    - `stand_masks_on_new_answers.rs`: a `canvas` call, summary and full, on the password fixture after a typed
      sentinel holds neither the sentinel nor `MASKED_VALUE` (test-plan · decision/typed-password-never-returned).
    - `stand_requirement_sweep.rs`: the witness strings at :560 and :854 take the renamed test names of steps 5 and 9
      (test-plan · decision/count-and-rename-sweeps).

15. **The binary's roles at trace** (`examples/seven_guis/tests/`).
    - `mcp_server.rs`:
      - the listing is the sixteen verbs of the table, `canvas` after `layout`, `help` last (:3, :132);
      - a `canvas` call on the Counter through the `mcp` role equals the command line's answer for the same id.
    - `host_log.rs` and `mcp_log.rs`: one `canvas` call each, summary and full, at `trace` under both builds, reads 0
      needles of `canvas_needles()` (obs-plan · decision/sink-host-read-at-trace; obs S1).
    - `common/mod.rs` gains `canvas_needles()`: the answer's keys `"kinds"`, `"digest"` and `"fonts"`, and the
      summary's digest as the in-process run writes it.

16. **The cold-agent pipe takes the tool** (`scripts/cold-agent.sh`, `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py`).
    - F1 B reaches the provider through MCP, and the pipe's `isolated` reads exactly the server's tools (test-plan ·
      contract/cold-agent-verdict/isolated).
    - `VERBS` (cold-agent.sh:54, test_cold_agent.py:23) takes `canvas` after `layout`.
    - `COUNTED` (:72) stays as it is, a comment stating why: no served app holds a canvas until «Cold-agent bar»
      (F5 B).
    - The fake's comment (test_cold_agent.py:100) and its tools read sixteen.
    - No live run is part of this chunk.

The gates:
- escher-driver's unit tests;
- the two new stand targets;
- the blitz-tests companions the diff moves;
- seven_guis' four process checks;
- the two CI-script tests;
- the lock guard;
- the pre-push gate (`fast`);

- the `audit` leg. escher-driver takes two dependencies; the fast leg runs no audit (security-plan ·
  decision/local-audit-before-push);
- `stand-repeat`. Both new targets are `stand_` files, so they run by its glob.
What is absent:

- No boot-path touchpoint changes a binary's start: `session_host.rs` is untouched. `cli_commands`, `mcp_server`,
  `host_log` and `mcp_log` drive both binaries' roles and stand in for the smoke.
- There is no live leg: the cold-agent pipe takes the tool into its lists and runs no live run.
- There is no headful self-verify harness in this project, and this is no UI chunk.

- The coverage leg is not run locally. CI's coverage job reads escher-driver's 97 % and blitz-test-harness's 90 %
  floors on the pushed tree, and the CI read below asserts green over it.

Each new check is controlled red-before-green (tests S4). After the steps are green, /implement makes four one-shot
`gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each names the edit's text and the case by its test name (gate-contract.md
§Control), and each enters with the red reading it must produce:

- **The read reaching a pass.**
  - Edit: the `Command::Canvas` arm in `execute.rs` calls `self.harness.pump()` before `self.canvas(id)`.
  - Fired on: the `stand_canvas_commands` entry, case `a_canvas_read_changes_nothing_with_timer_ticks_pending`.
  - Red reading: the delivered ticks read applied after the call, `timer-elapsed`'s name moving.

- **Glyph ids written.**
  - Edit: `json.rs` writes the `glyphs` line's `ids=` as the glyph ids joined by `,` in place of the digest.
  - Fired on: the new-targets entry, case `the_fixtures_answers_hold_no_glyph_id_and_no_text`.
  - Red reading: the `ids` value is not 16 lowercase hex.

- **Exploration's canvas filter removed.**
  - Edit: `explorable` in `explore.rs` no longer leaves out the `Commands` and `CommandCounts` kinds.
  - Fired on: the escher-driver unit entry, case
    `the_verbs_explored_are_the_tables_target_verbs_with_no_image_no_layout_and_no_canvas_reading`.
  - Red reading: `canvas` among the explored verbs.

- **The budget doubled.**
  - Edit: the canvas cut in `execute.rs` measures parts against `2 * SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`. A control removing a bound
    loosens it to twice the budget (test-plan · decision/mutation-controlled-tests).
  - Fired on: the `stand_canvas_commands` entry, case `a_full_dump_over_the_budget_reads_in_parts_each_within_it`.
  - Red reading: a part over 10,000 bytes and the 100-circle dump read in fewer parts than its table row.

An acceptance reads CI: the windows and macOS legs hold the canvas table and the re-read `actions` digests, and CI's
coverage job holds the floors. So the operator's hygiene, push and CI entries stand. The diff is OS-sensitive in two
ways, and the `ci.py` entry's note names both:

- the `cfg(unix)` items of the new socket and kept-check tests: the windows leg runs the in-process and MCP tests
  alone;
- the committed digest tables.

body:
- (engine) `blitz_paint::custom_widget_scene` reads one widget's recorded commands outside a raster, behind
  `custom-widget`, in a function of escher's own, `paint_scene` and `build_custom_widget_scenes` unedited (architecture
  · decision/fork-additions-in-own-functions; F9 A). Proven by the new-targets entry through the driver's read.

- (driver) `canvas` is the sixteenth verb, a `VERBS` row at the instance level after `layout`.
  - It takes a required `id`, an optional `full` flag and an optional `part`, and validates through `validate`:
    accepted with an id, `malformed` without one, past `MAX_ID_BYTES`, with a part of 0 or 1001, or with an argument
    it does not take.
  - It adds no cause, session error, exit status, node key or argument kind (architecture ·
    contract/driver-verbs/verb-table, contract/argument-kinds/flag; security-plan · decision/closed-driver-verb-schema).
  - Proven by `cargo test -p escher-driver --locked --lib`.

- (driver) Circle Drawer's canvas, read in process in both layout modes:
  - It answers a summary (`canvas`, content-box size, counts per kind, depth, digest) and a full dump of one line per
    command.

title: evidence/founder-forks.md
body:
# Forks — Canvas draw commands (2026-11-24-canvas-draw-commands)

Written at P4, before any plan, on the operator's take-up directive (inputs#I1): every fork, what crosses, the rule it
meets, each option's measured cost, the dependences, and the most conservative option that still builds the entry.
**No default is taken: every fork stands open.** Nothing here is applied.

The entry: «a driver verb answering a canvas's commands, summary and full levels, deterministic, diffable; size
measured; every carrier's crossing the founder's fork (v040-10)». The stand's one canvas is Circle Drawer's.

## What exists (measured at HEAD `8520d7743`)
- A widget paints into an anyrender `Scene` (`Widget::paint -> Scene`). `paint_scene` builds every widget's scene into
  a map local to the call and drops it after the paint (`packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs:54-61,83-145`), so no read
  outside a paint sees a canvas's commands today. Any option needs a new read in blitz-paint behind `custom-widget`.
- A `Scene` is `{tolerance, commands}`. There are eight command kinds: `PushLayer`, `PushClipLayer`, `PushMaskLayer`,
  `PopLayer`, `Stroke`, `Fill`, `GlyphRun`, `BoxShadow` (anyrender 0.15.0, `src/recording.rs:18-41,184-187`).
- A `GlyphRun` holds glyph ids with their x and y, the font size, a brush and **the whole font's bytes**. It holds no
  text (`recording.rs:147-166`).
- Circle Drawer paints one clip layer over its content box. Per circle it paints one `Fill` (the disc), one `Stroke`
  (the ring) and its diameter as glyph runs, each glyph origin rounded to a whole device pixel, then one `PopLayer`
  (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs:140-185`). Its canvas text is numbers only (F3 A of
  2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas).
- Circle Drawer boots in process only and is served by no `escher-session` role (arch `contract/headless-stand/boot`,
  F1 A of 2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas, to be served at «Cold-agent bar», v040-15).
- **The yardstick for a new verb on every carrier:** the last one, `layout` (2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers,
  `3802fe16d^..c7c09a7bf`), changed 32 files with +1342 −124 lines under `packages examples tests docs README.md
  .github` (`git diff --stat`).
- **The dump's size is now measured** (§Readings, below). The estimate written here first is superseded.

## The rules every crossing meets
- **R1 — canvas content crosses as pixels alone.** Arch `decision/canvas-crosses-as-pixels` and security
  `decision/canvas-content-crosses-as-shot-pixels`, both ratified: «with no new carrier, verb, field, exit, refusal
  cause, session error, log field or span».
- **R2 — the boundary widening rule.** Security `decision/boundary-widening-rule`: a closed-value field in a ratified
  carrier is no widening; authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit is. The playbook pattern
  `rul-izni57qv` (Boundary widening) holds a wrap on it, always a human's call.
- **R3 — a verb joins only by ratification.** Arch `decision/validated-verb-set-widened-by-ratification`. A verb in
  `VERBS` crosses the session socket, the command line and MCP by construction (arch
  `contract/driver-session/schema-carriers`) and is kept in a recorded check (`contract/kept-check/kept-verbs`).
- **R4 — answers written by the driver's own writer.** Arch `decision/answers-written-by-own-json-writer`,
  `decision/hand-written-answers` and `decision/serde-json-reader-only`, all ratified: no serialization crate writes
  an answer; serde_json reads only.
- **R5 — what an MCP client does onward is the client's.** Security `decision/mcp-results-client-responsibility`. A
  cold-agent live run carries what the MCP server answers to the model provider
  (`decision/cold-agent-screen-to-provider`). So «to the provider» follows from «over MCP» unless the cold-agent pipe
  filters the tool.
- **R6 — nothing of a screen in a log.** Arch `contract/command-span/never-fielded`: a read verb's command span
  records `verb` and, refused, `cause` alone.

---

## F1 — Where the read may cross (the carriers) · the founder's
**What crosses:** a canvas's app-painted content as data: shapes, colours, transforms and, per F3, its text in some
form. Today it crosses as pixels alone (R1).

| | Option | Rule met | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **In process only** — `Session::canvas(id, level)` returning a typed value, as `explore` is today. No verb, no carrier. | None: nothing leaves the process; R1 stands. | The read and its checks alone. No schema, CLI, MCP, recording, `help`, capability-statement or README change. |
| B | **The sixteenth verb on every ratified carrier** — the session socket, the command line, MCP and a kept check; to the model provider only through MCP, on a live cold-agent run (R5). | Reverses R1 for every carrier; R3 (a verb joins); R2 (pattern `rul-izni57qv`). | The `layout` yardstick: 32 files, +1342 −124. The verb count moves 15 → 16 on `docs/capabilities.md`, README and `test_capability_statement.py`. |
| C | **A verb on the socket and the command line, no MCP tool** — kept out of the provider's reach by construction. | Reverses R1 for two carriers; R3; breaks the one schema on every carrier (`contract/driver-session/schema-carriers`) and `tools/list`'s «the fifteen verbs» (`contract/mcp-server/tools-list`) — a second rule change. | B's cost plus a split listing in `mcp.rs` and `describe.rs`, and a stated asymmetry in `help`. |

**Most conservative that still builds the entry: B.** A builds the read but not «a driver verb … every carrier's
crossing», since no carrier carries it. C needs a second rule broken to keep one carrier out. B is the one shape the
schema already has. Its exposure is narrowed by F3 and F4, not by carrier.

**Depends on:** F3 and F4 set what B carries. F5 decides whether B can be proven on the stand. Under A, F5 and F7 fall
away.

## F2 — Who writes the dump · a decisive lean (R4), listed so it can be reopened
| | Option | Rule met | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **Hand-written by the driver's own writer** (`json.rs`), one line or object per command, a field per closed kind. | None. | Eight command kinds' writers. No dependency added (`cargo tree`: anyrender's `serde` feature reads off in the driver's graph). |
| B | **anyrender's serde derives, written by serde_json.** | Reverses R4 (serde_json becomes a writer). Turns on anyrender's, kurbo's and peniko's `serde` features in the driver's graph. | The `serde` feature on three crates already in the graph. serde_json's writer path is newly used. |
| C | **`anyrender_serialize`**, the workspace's scene archiver. | Reverses R4. Writes a zip archive (`resources.json`, `draw_commands.json`, PNGs, WOFF2 fonts), not a line. | **+44 crates** to the driver's graph (94 under it, 44 absent today: zip, brotli, sha2, gif, image-webp, zune-jpeg, ttf2woff2, write-fonts, skera, clap and its parsers among them). Each one also enters the audit leg's licence and advisory read. |

**Most conservative that still builds: A.** An artifact settles it, so it is a lean and not a question unless the
founder wants R4 reopened.

## F3 — What a glyph run carries · the founder's (R2: authored text)
**What crosses:** the text an app draws inside a canvas. On the stand that is Circle Drawer's diameters, numbers only.
At 0.4.0's later samples it is node titles and port names (v040-14).

| | Option | Rule met | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **No text in any form** — per glyph run its glyph count, font size, bounding box, brush and a 64-bit FNV-1a digest of its glyph ids. A changed label shows in the diff as a changed digest. | B's carriers reverse R1, but this field is closed values only (numbers and a digest): no authored text crosses (R2). | One digest per run, using the same FNV-1a 64 the kept check already writes (`contract/kept-check/digest`). A digest of masked text is banned in kept checks; canvas text is not masked text, so that ban does not reach it — stated here for the founder. |
| B | **Glyph ids and positions**, the font by reference (F4). | Authored text in another spelling: a reader with the font maps ids back to text (R2 widening). | Per glyph an id and two numbers; size grows with the text's length. |
| C | **The text itself**, recovered from the font's cmap (or handed by the widget through a new `Widget` method). | Authored text as text (R2 widening). Through B's MCP carrier it reaches the model provider (R5). | cmap reversal is many-to-one for some glyphs (ligatures, shaping), so the text is not always exact. The other route is a `Widget` API addition, an engine change for every document behind `custom-widget`, flagged upstreamable. |

**Most conservative that still builds: A.** It is deterministic, diffable (the digest moves when a label changes) and
carries no text. Two limits: an agent cannot read a label's words from the dump (the screenshot still shows them), and
two labels with the same glyph ids read the same.

**Depends on:** F1 (under F1 A the text never leaves the process, and C costs no widening). F4 (B needs the font by
reference). «Canvas lint» (the next entry) needs a label's bounding box, which every option carries, not its text.

## F4 — How the heavy data is named · the operator's (closed values; no widening under R2)
**What crosses:** which font and which image a command uses. The font's bytes ride every glyph run today.

| | Option | Rule met | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **An index into the dump's own resource list plus a 64-bit FNV-1a digest of the bytes**, never the bytes. | None beyond F1's. | One digest per distinct font or image per read. The bundled DejaVu Sans is the stand's only font (arch `decision/stand-typography-dejavu-sans`). |
| B | **The font's family name** as the font reports it. | Text from a font file, an open value set (R2), though on the stand it is always «DejaVu Sans». | A name read from the font's tables. |
| C | **Omitted** — glyph runs carry no font reference. | None. | Two runs at one size in two fonts read alike. |

**Most conservative that still builds: A.**

## F5 — Where the carriers are proven · the founder's (it reopens his F1 A of 2026-11-23)
**What crosses:** nothing new by itself. It decides whether a stand canvas reaches a carrier in this chunk.

| | Option | Rule met | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **Serve Circle Drawer now**, the eighth served task. | Reverses his F1 A of 2026-11-23 («не сейчас», served at v040-15). The served list moves 7 → 8 (arch `contract/escher-session/invocation`, `contract/escher-session-cli/usage`). The cold-agent pipe's app set grows. | `session_host.rs` `TASKS`, the served tables in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`, `stand_cross_os_readings`' served set, `docs/capabilities.md`'s count and its pin. Circle Drawer's text-holding shot stays outside every cross-OS byte check. |
| B | **Prove the carriers on a test-only canvas fixture** served by a test host, Circle Drawer staying in process. | None beyond F1's. A served fixture is test-only, as `select_popup`'s pages are. | A fixture page with a widget, and a host boot in the test's shared module. No served count moves. |
| C | **Prove the carriers by the writer's unit tests and one in-process `Session::run`**; no process carrier exercised end to end. | None beyond F1's. | Least code. The acceptance «the crossing the founder ruled holds on every carrier» is then proven in process for MCP and the CLI writer, not through the binary. |

**Most conservative that still builds: B.** It keeps his F1 A and still runs the binary on a canvas. C keeps it too
but leaves the carriers unexercised as processes.

**Depends on:** F1. Only B or C of F1 needs it.

## F6 — The summary level's content · the operator's (closed values; no widening)
| | Option | Rule met | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **Counts per command kind, the canvas's content-box size, the layer depth and one 64-bit digest of the full dump.** | None beyond F1's. | A fixed handful of numbers: constant size at any canvas size. |
| B | **A digest of the full dump alone.** | None beyond F1's. | One number. An agent learns «changed» but not what kind changed. |

**Most conservative that still builds: A.** B is smaller but serves «a summary level» less.

## F7 — A dump over the 10,000-byte budget · the operator's
| | Option | Rule met | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **Parts of whole commands**, the optional `part` argument as `snapshot` and `graph` take it (1 to `MAX_PART` = 1000; arch `decision/large-screen-in-parts`). | None beyond F1's. The pattern is ratified for two verbs and needs no new argument kind. | The graph's paging code, reused. A part never splits a layer's push from its pop: a part carries its open layers' depth. |
| B | **No paging** — a full dump over the budget is answered whole within the 1,048,576-byte answer bound. | None. | No code. It may pass an agent client's token warning (the reason for the budget, arch `decision/snapshot-text-budget`). |
| C | **Refuse past the budget** under an existing cause. | No existing cause means it; a new one reverses `decision/refusal-causes-closed-at-eight`. | A cause or a reused one that misreads. |

**Most conservative that still builds: A.** Whether Circle Drawer ever passes the budget is unmeasured (§What exists).
The node graph (v040-14) is the likelier canvas to pass it.

**Depends on:** F1 (only a crossing verb answers in parts) and the probe's size measurement.

## F8 — The verb's call shape · the operator's
| | Option | Rule met | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **`canvas --id <id> [--full] [--part n]`**: the summary by default, `--full` a flag (an existing argument kind). | R3 (one verb). | No new argument kind; kinds stay seven (`contract/argument-kinds`). |
| B | **`canvas --id <id> --level summary|full`**: a closed-word argument. | R3, plus an eighth argument kind. | The argument kinds' table, the validation order and `help` grow. |
| C | **An argument on `screenshot`** (`--as commands`). | It changes a ratified verb's answer shape and its MCP image-block result (`contract/mcp-role/screenshot-result`). | Two answer shapes behind one verb. The kept check's shot-without-pixels rule becomes conditional. |

**Most conservative that still builds: A.** The verb's name is the founder's to change.

**Depends on:** F1 B.

## F9 — The engine read · the operator's (no behaviour change)
| | Option | Rule met | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **A public read in blitz-paint behind `custom-widget`, in a function of escher's own** (arch `decision/fork-additions-in-own-functions`). It hands the widget its fonts and calls `Widget::paint` once more for one node, outside a raster, and returns its `Scene`. Flagged upstreamable. | An API addition; no document's behaviour changes. | One function beside `process_custom_widget_node`. A widget's `paint` then runs once per read as well as once per shot. |
| B | **Keep the widget scenes a paint built** (a map on the document), read after a shot. | It changes `paint_scene` for every document behind the feature. | A read only answers after a paint. It is stale between a step and the next shot. |

**Most conservative that still builds: A.**

---

## Dependences, in one line each
- F1 decides the rest. Under A, F5, F7 and F8 fall away, and F3 costs no widening.
- F3 and F4 together decide what B of F1 carries to MCP and, through it, to the model provider (R5).
- F5 only matters under B or C of F1. Its A reverses his F1 A of 2026-11-23.
- F7 waits on the probe's size measurement.
- F2 and F9 are leans an artifact settles. They are listed so the founder can reopen them, not because they are open
  by the rules.

## The conservative set, read together
F1 B · F2 A · F3 A · F4 A · F5 B · F6 A · F7 A · F8 A · F9 A. This is a sixteenth verb on every carrier, answering
closed values and digests only: no authored text, no font bytes, no family name. It is hand-written, paged like
`graph`, proven on a test-only served canvas, and Circle Drawer stays unserved. It still reverses R1 for every carrier,
which is a boundary widening (`rul-izni57qv`) and the founder's alone to answer. Nothing here is taken as a default.

## The operator's answers (inputs#I2)
F2 A · F4 A · F6 A · F7 A (to be re-read once the size is measured; re-read below) · F8 A · F9 A. F1, F3 and F5 are the
founder's and stay open: no default.

## Readings — the probe (inputs#I2's measurement)
**Where it ran.** A throwaway worktree `../escher-probe-canvas-dump`, outside `target/`, on branch
`build/probe-canvas-dump` at `b25a9c5e3` (pushed to origin), cut from `8520d7743`. Nothing went on the version branch,
and nothing is deleted.

**What it holds.**
- The F9 A read: `blitz_paint::custom_widget_scene(doc, node, scale)`, 9 lines in `packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs`
  behind `custom-widget`. It calls the existing `process_custom_widget_node` with a fresh recording `Scene` as its
  render context.
- A hand-written dump (F2 A) in one test target, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/probe_canvas_dump.rs`:
  - One line per command, layers as indentation. Shapes are SVG path text, numbers are rounded to 1/1000 and written
    shortest, colours are `#rrggbbaa`, and transforms are `id` or six numbers.
  - Fonts by index plus an FNV-1a 64 digest of their bytes (F4 A).
  - The summary (F6 A) is one JSON line: counts per kind, the content box, the deepest layer, and the digest of the
    form-A dump.
- The glyph-run forms:
  - **F3 A:** `n`, the origins' box and a digest of the glyph ids.
  - **F3 B:** `id@x,y` per glyph.
  - **F3 C:** the origins' box and the text recovered from the font's cmap through skrifa. It read «59» for a 59-px
    circle, exact on the stand's digits.
- **How the circles were set.** Circle Drawer is booted through `seven_guis::stand::boot_circle_drawer`. Its canvas's
  `data-circles` is set to n circles from a fixed sequence: whole-pixel centres, diameters 10–79, in its 696 × 396
  content box. The scene is read at scale 1.0.

**Bytes of the dump text** (the same in both layout modes; the bytes as a JSON string in brackets):

| circles | full, F3 A | full, F3 B | full, F3 C | summary (F6 A) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 555 (562) | 540 (547) | 540 (549) | 152 (182) |
| 12 | 5,426 (5,466) | 5,246 (5,286) | 5,246 (5,310) | 155 (185) |
| 100 | 44,993 (45,297) | 43,493 (43,797) | 43,493 (43,997) | 158 (188) |

- About 450 B per circle at a full level, almost all of it the disc's and the ring's path text: 4 cubic segments each,
  about 190 B per path. The glyph run is 60–80 B of a circle's line set.
- The three F3 forms differ by under 4 %. F3 A is the largest by its fixed 16-hex digest. F3 B and F3 C are equal in
  bytes at these diameters, which are two digits each.
- The summary stays between 152 and 158 B at any count.

**Cross-OS.** All 24 readings (3 counts × 4 forms × 2 layout modes) are held to one committed table of bytes and
FNV-1a 64 digests, taken on linux x86_64. CI#45403397213 at `b25a9c5e3` concluded `success`, 17/17 jobs.
`probe_dump_matches_its_table ... ok` was read in `Test [default features]` (linux), `Test (windows)` and
`Test (macos)`, and in `Coverage report`. **Every dump is byte-equal on linux, windows and macOS**, in both layout
modes, in all three F3 forms and the summary.

**What this does to the forks.**
- **F7 re-read.** The 10,000-byte budget holds about 22 circles at a full level: 12 circles read 5,426 B, 100 circles
  read 44,993 B. A full dump of a busy canvas passes the budget, and the node graph (v040-14) will too. So F7 A's
  paging is needed, not hypothetical. The answer A stands as given. The summary never approaches the budget.
- **F3.** Size does not separate the three options: they are within 4 % of each other. Determinism does not separate
  them either: all three are byte-equal on the three hosts. What separates them is only what crosses — R2's authored
  text, as the section above states.
- **F1.** Under B, 12 circles answer about 5.4 KB as one whole answer and 100 circles about 45 KB in five parts. Both
  are far inside the 1,048,576-byte answer bound.
- **F9 A** holds as designed: a read outside a raster, the widget painted once more. Its tests and the rest of the
  workspace stayed green on the same run.

## Beside the forks (observations, not forks)
- watch `cry-em4q2mag` (1/3): an observation. No fork, criterion or plan step attaches to it.
- matrix#v040-10's acceptance also holds the canvas lint and the grouping by virtual node, which «Canvas lint» and
  «Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes» list. This chunk advances the cap and is not expected to claim it.

- Disabled-ness is keyed one way since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (in every document, ratified by the founder): the `DISABLED` state (`:disabled`) reads the attribute's presence, and the pointer-move gate, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate, the Enter and Space activation and focusability read `ElementData::is_disabled` — that presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea` alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable, a bare `disabled` set after creation takes its focusability away, and a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus. dioxus-native-dom removes a falsy value of its 28 boolean attributes — upstream's `is_bool_attr` predicate since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (`disabled`, `checked`, `hidden`, `inert` among them; a framework-written `inert: false` is removed, while a truthy `inert` (by presence on itself or an ancestor element) takes focusability, hits and the tree away from its subtree (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) and Tab reaches the buttons under `inert: false`; HTML's focus fixup is built, in every document, so a node holding focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives focus up as the mutator flushes, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing; and a focused node that no longer shows gives focus up after each layout, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing, while a `display: contents` control and one beside a hidden sibling keep focus (ratified, the Tab walk's skip of unshown nodes remedying the Tab trap the post-layout fixup alone made; a control whose own `:focus-within` rule hides its container still takes Tab and loses focus at the next layout, a stated limit)), so a `hidden: false` element stays displayed, in the tree and in the snapshot; an attribute outside the list holding `false` is still written as `"false"`. The snapshot reads `enabled` by presence — the driver's `disabled` refusal cause is stated on the same presence reading ("the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled") and is detected on it and on nothing else: the driver refuses a `click` or a `type` as `disabled` when the snapshot reads the element not enabled, with nothing dispatched and focus as it was, and acts on the same control once it reads enabled (`stand_act_disabled.rs`), and the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's state, else, on a checkable role, the node's `toggled` reading (`True` true, `False` and `Mixed` false; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and `value` from the element (a `select`'s `value` `BaseDocument::select_value` — the chosen option's value, for a `multiple` select its first chosen option's in tree order, nothing with none chosen — its options, its children and those under an `optgroup`, kept in the tree as `ListBoxOption` nodes, each `selected` from its chosen state, a closed drop-down's options under it with its select's client rect as their `bounds`, which the driver's visual lint leaves out of its overlap reading in every document with an open list's rows and groups, an open list's row reading its painted row's `bounds` (`Entry.in_select_box`, read through `closed_select_of` for a closed select's option and through `select_list_bounds` for an open list's row or group, never the role) — the stand's flight booker at boot no `overlap`, `stand_lint` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]` — while a list box's rows and groups, `multiple` or of display size above 1, read their own client rects and its rows are linted as usual; a range input's `value` its current value since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction — `ElementData::range_input_value`, the formatted value a key or a pointerdown moved, while its `value` attribute keeps the boot value; a password input's value reads the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE` where it holds text and `""` where it holds none, a file input's where its `value` attribute is non-empty — and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a password's typed text is in no painted frame either: blitz-paint paints its value as bullets, its caret at the bullet of its caret index, in every document and through every renderer that paints with blitz-paint, windowed included (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12), two values of one length painting byte-identical frames, focused or not, in both layout modes (`password_painted_masked.rs`); a click inside a field holding a value places the caret by the bullets — `click_password_input` lays out one U+2022 per character through `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input`, finds the bullet under the point and moves the real editor to that character, so no width of the real characters reaches the caret: two values of one length read one index, in both layout modes (`password_caret_click.rs`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the windowed paint is not run; a textarea's typed text reads back as its `value`, proven on an in-file fixture where it is named by `aria-label`), and `focused` from the tree, and `clickable` (a `bool` after `focused`, true where the vdom walk's current listeners hold `click` and the element is no disabled form control; `Snapshot::to_text` writes the token `clickable` after `focused` only when true, and `Snapshot::diff` reads it as `Reading::Clickable`) — focus proven after a click, a Tab press and Shift+Tab (`stand_snapshot_state.rs`). The snapshot's text form (`Snapshot::to_text`) reads that model, never the tree or a control: one line per node, its role and name the node's, with no second mapping (`stand_snapshot_text.rs`). The text's parts (`Snapshot::text_parts`, `TextPart`) are one more reader of that model through the text form and of nothing else — consecutive pre-order lines of `to_text`, never a split line, the parts concatenating to the whole text with every node id on exactly one line — and the driver's `snapshot` reads a screen over `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` in parts: on an over-budget fixture, in both layout modes, each part's lines equal their lines in the whole text, a password's line reads `MASKED_VALUE` in every part, and exactly one line reads `focused` after a click (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`). The snapshot's diff (`Snapshot::diff`) is one more reader of that model: a text change is reported on the element whose accessible name it changes, by its id and never as a text-run entry, a hidden element leaves and returns with its descendants, and a focus move names exactly the controls whose `focused` reading moved (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface an MCP tool result is one more reader of that model and of nothing else — a `snapshot` result is `to_text`'s output itself for a whole screen, equal byte for byte to `Session::run`'s screen text in both layout modes (`stand_mcp_tools.rs`), and, for a screen read in parts, its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` holding that part's text — through `serve_mcp` a walk's text blocks equal the JSON lines `Session::run` writes, in both layout modes (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`), its crossing to an MCP client ratified by the founder (2026-10-10). Since 2026-10-12-self-description a password input typed through an MCP `type` reads `MASKED_VALUE` in the tool result, role `PasswordInput` and a non-empty name, the typed text in neither result, in both layout modes — a test-only element of the shared password page `fixtures::password_named` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs`), no stand task or app gaining one; and two further readers of the same model state closed words only: the node keys' help that `help` serves (each key's reading, the boolean model's two limits among them) and `DiffNode::differs`, a changed node naming the readings that differ from before the step in node-key order — the Flight Booker's Book names eight nodes — seven that only moved, each `differs` = `[bounds]`, and since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness `flight-book` itself, which the click now focuses, `differs` = `[focused, bounds]` (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the driver's `screenshot` is one more reader of the model's bounds and of nothing else in it — an element shot, addressed by stable id and refused as every id-addressed call is, is the node's bounds rounded outward and cropped to the part that can be seen — and a shot changes nothing: no focus moves, `has_changes` stays false and the next diff is empty, in both layout modes (`stand_act_screenshot.rs`). The canvas read, which reads one canvas element's draw commands (Circle Drawer's circles and diameter labels leaving only as shot pixels and as the canvas verb's draw commands, no label's text among them), is no reader of the snapshot model. Since 2026-11-07-ui-graph the read-only UI graph (`DioxusDocument::graph`, a `UiGraph`, behind `accessibility`) is one more reader beside the snapshot: one `GraphNode` per snapshot node in pre-order, carrying ids, component names, state names, handler event names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value, with no second role or name mapping — `stand_graph` asserts in both layout modes that every graph node is a snapshot node and that a graph read changes nothing and holds no typed text. Since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here the driver's `actions` verb (`Session::actions`) is one more read-only reader: for every actionable node (`DioxusDocument::actionable_nodes`, each an `ActionableNode` of `id`, `owner` and `keyed`, read through the one crate-private actionable rule `Readings` it shares with `unkeyed_actionable` — focusable, one of 27 interactive roles, or current vdom-walk listeners holding an event other than `mounted`, so a listener a re-render removed is read by neither) it answers each id-taking verb with the cause `check_target` would refuse it with, changing nothing and writing ids, owner ids, verb and cause words and booleans only, never a value; `keyed` on the carriers is standing — the actionable-key check's wire form, true where the id holds no slash, and Cells' unpaged answer (678 nodes, 106,088 bytes) is a stated limit owned by residual `res-7cc5bi4k`.

- `Document::accessibility_tree` (gated `accessibility`) is what the shell builds — on InitialTreeRequested and, in a redraw after style resolve, when the document's changed set taken there was non-empty, a poll pushing no tree (`changed_nodes`, the nodes written since the last `take_changed_nodes` — a scroll that closes a select's list and its highlight moving to another row marking it, node creation, hover, active, any other scroll and layout alone marking none, a focus lost after a layout marking it; a harness settle neither reads nor drains it and a fresh harness document's set is non-empty, so a check reading `has_changes()` as "this step changed something" drains first) (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07, its windowed witness, at the platform adapter, still owed and owned by residual `res-llkgqygv` (re-carried at 0.3.0, target: next), an active assistive technology this version does not reach, on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), both halves proven headlessly on the stand since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions; before 2026-10-07 the refresh on change never ran); a `DioxusDocument` overrides it to set each element node's `author_id` to its stable element id — none on `TextRun`, document-root or `Window` nodes. The workspace pins the Dioxus crates `default-features = false`: the override — and the snapshot model built on it (`DioxusDocument::snapshot`, which takes role, name and focus from this tree, never a second mapping; its text form `Snapshot::to_text`, that text's parts `Snapshot::text_parts` and its diff `Snapshot::diff` read that model and map nothing again, as does the read-only UI graph `DioxusDocument::graph`, a `UiGraph` of one node per snapshot node, names and closed words only — the canvas read, which reads one canvas element's draw commands, being no reader of the snapshot model —, while the `signal_registry` module (`use_graph_state`, `DeclaredWrite`, `SignalRegistry`) and the reached-handler record (`record_reached`, `reached_handlers`) are not gated) — exists only where a crate names `dioxus-native-dom/accessibility` or depends on one that does (blitz-tests and escher-driver name it; seven_guis names none and gets it through escher-driver, so both its binaries compile these modules — with no platform adapter, so the stand binary still gives no assistive technology a tree). An AccessKit `Adapter` is created before the window is first shown — it panics if the window is already visible.

- `paint_scene(PaintScene, &mut BaseDocument, scale, width, height, x_offset, y_offset)`, which calls `paint_select_list` after the root's render and before the devtools overlays, an open select's list read from `SelectListView` and past any clip or `opacity` on its select's ancestors and past the blend layers, reaching a shell or renderer through `paint_scene` alone; and, behind the `custom-widget` feature beside `build_custom_widget_scenes`, `custom_widget_scene`, which returns one custom widget's scene outside a raster at a given scale (an escher addition flagged upstreamable).

- escher-driver (native target only): the second binary, `escher-session <verb> [arguments] --session <dir>` (`src/session_host.rs`), is the driver's command line over seven served tasks — the four lean ones, Cells, the load page and the order page — and the one place a served task, the stand's boot and the timer's tick handle meet a driver `Session` — `main` installs the telemetry sink first, then hands argv, the seven slugs `counter` · `flight-booker` · `timer` · `crud` · `cells` · `load` · `order` (a private `TASKS` table, from which the usage line's `apps:` and the MCP `start` tool's `enum` are written) and the stand's boot to `escher_driver::command_line`; the boot starts a session through `stand` only (Cells through `stand::boot_cells`, the load page through `stand::boot_load`) and hands the timer's session its time step (`stand::timer_step` over the tick handle, through `Session::with_time`; the other six carry none and still take `advance`, which moves their session's clock alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18)). `start <task> [--record <dir>]` checks its recording directory itself before it spawns, then spawns the same binary in its host role, `serve <task> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]` (passing `--record` to the host); since 2026-10-19-session-recording `--record <dir>`, taken at most once on `start`, the host role and the `mcp` role, keeps the session as one owner-only replayable check — `check-{n}.json` (`0600`, never replacing a file) in a `0700` directory whose parent must exist, removed by escher only when its recording fails, holding per call its verb, arguments, acceptance, the answer's digest and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, the answer itself as an `answer` key — the line the driver wrote, masked as on every carrier, a shot's kept as `{"width":…,"height":…}` without its `png` — read back and replayed by `Check::replay` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19: F1 A · F2 B, F3 B) — a directory open to its group or others refused as the session error `record-dir-not-private` (exit 3, `start` spawning nothing), a recording that ends answering `recording-failed` (exit 3; over MCP `isError`); the host serves until `stop` or its 30-minute idle expiry and writes nothing to stdout; every other command is one client run that answers one line of JSON on stdout (exit `0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error — the four read from `EXIT_STATUSES` and served by `help`), save `help` (since 2026-10-12-self-description), which needs no `--session` — it admits at most one and reads it not — and answers the tool's self-description with status `0`, reaching no session; the `mcp` role lists it as its sixteenth tool, last, `graph` after `lint`, `actions` after `graph`, `layout` after `actions` and `canvas` after `layout`. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the seventh instance verb, `screenshot [--id <id>] --session <dir>`, answers one uncoloured line `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}` on stdout, exit 0 — the whole screen, or with `--id` the element cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen — an app with no font it can paint text with refused `fonts-unavailable` and an element shot that crops to no pixel `off-screen`, exit 1; over the `mcp` role an accepted shot is an `image` block (`image/png`, base64) then a text block, the line without `png`. The eighth instance verb, `lint --session <dir>`, takes no argument (one named refused `malformed`) and answers one uncoloured line `{"findings":[…]}` on stdout, exit 0, each finding keyed `id` · `defect` · `bounds` then its reason's keys — ids, closed words and numbers only — an app with no font it can paint text with refused `fonts-unavailable`, exit 1, a `lint` step kept under `--record` like every instance verb; over the `mcp` role an accepted `lint` answers its JSON line of findings as one text block. The ninth instance verb, `graph [--part <part>] --session <dir>`, after `lint`, takes one optional `--part`, a whole number from 1 to 1000 (a part of 0, of 1001 or of text refused `malformed` with nothing run) and answers one uncoloured line `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}` on stdout, exit 0, whole when no part is asked and the answer is within the 10,000-byte snapshot text budget, else in parts of whole nodes adding `part` and `parts` — part 1 alone carrying the states, a later part's empty states meaning read part 1, a part past the last empty nodes and states — carrying ids, component names, handler event names, registered state names, closed flag words, booleans and the part counts only, never a value; over the `mcp` role an accepted `graph` answers its JSON line `{"nodes","states"}` (a part's adding `part` and `parts`) as one text block. The tenth instance verb, `actions --session <dir>`, after `graph`, takes no argument (one named refused `malformed`) and answers one uncoloured line `{"nodes":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"keyed":…,"verbs":[{"verb":…,"cause":…}]}]}` on stdout, exit 0, `owner` and `cause` left out when absent, carrying ids, owner ids, the table's verb words, closed cause words and booleans only, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`, the answer unpaged; over the `mcp` role an accepted `actions` answers its JSON line `{"nodes"}` as one text block. one definition of what can be asked of the driver and of how it says no, the **executor** that runs a call on the held instance, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli the **command line** that carries a call recording directory keeps its answered calls at rest as one owner-only replayable check (`std` only, unix only like the socket), and since 2026-10-19-visual-lint the **visual lint** (`Session::lint` in process and the `lint` verb, the eighth instance verb, on every carrier (the socket's `call`, the command line, an MCP tool, `help`'s listing) and recorded — built by «Visual lint» (its gated Past 400 records or 1,048,576 bytes, or on a failed write, the recording ends — its check removed, the call not rolled back — and `Session::recording_failed(&mut self) -> bool` reads true once. `Check::from_bytes(&[u8]) -> Result<Check, Refusal>` reads a kept check strictly — since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `answer` required and a JSON object (missing, a string, a number, an array or `null` refused; key order not enforced, as for every key) — anything else refused `Cause::Malformed` with no fault, nothing of the file held and no panic path, building each `Call` through `command::call_of`; `Check::{app, steps}` and `Step::{call, accepted, digest, masked}` read it, the kept answer held in a private field read by `pub(crate) fn answer`, no public accessor returning a `serde_json` type. Since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `Check::replay(&self, session: &mut Session) -> Replay` (since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage through the crate-private `Check::replay_each(&self, session, after_step: impl FnMut(&Session)) -> Replay` with a no-op hook, its behaviour unchanged, `handler_coverage` the hook's other caller) runs nothing on a session whose `label()` is not the check's `app()`; otherwise it runs each step's `call()` through `Session::run`, so every step is validated again, and stops at the first step that differs — its acceptance differs, or the live answer's kept line, read by `serde_json::from_str`, is not equal to the kept `answer`; `Replay` (`holds()` · `another_app()` · `ran()` · `change() -> Option<&Change>`) and `Change` (`step()` · `accepted_then()` · `accepted_now()` · `keys() -> &[&'static str]`, the step verb's result fields that differ in table order, then `refused`) hold no reading and no `serde_json` type and derive `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq`; the module opens no span, each replayed step leaving its own `command` span. Since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage the public `handler_coverage(checks: &[Check], boot: impl FnMut() -> Result<Session, SessionError>) -> Result<Coverage, SessionError>` boots a fresh session for each check; a check whose app is not the label runs nothing and contributes nothing, and for each other it calls `record_reached()`, reads the UI graph at boot and after each replayed step through `Check::replay_each` (`mounted` left out, deduplicated by id and event) and adds `reached_handlers()` after the replay; it returns `Coverage { unexercised: Vec<HandlerRef>, checks: usize, held: usize }` with `HandlerRef { id, owner: Option<String>, event }`, both re-exported, written by hand by `Coverage::to_json` as `{"unexercised":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"event":…}],"checks":n,"held":m}`, `owner` left out when absent and `serde_json` writing nothing; its limits: handlers inside a canvas are not counted (deferred to 0.4.0), a handler on no screen a replay reached is not listed, and a bubbling dispatch that still propagates counts every listener it passed, and one a listener stops, or a handler's panic unwinds, counts its innermost listener alone, and a non-bubbling event counts its target alone.

- `Session::act(step) -> Result<Settled, SessionError>` — runs the closure on the held instance, then settles it (`Harness::settle`) and, since 2026-10-20-load-wait, through the load wait (crate-private `settle_waiting`): while the answer is `NotSettled { busy: Busy::Loads }` it settles again every `LOAD_POLL` (10 ms, private) until the load is answered, a failed load answering it, or `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time, re-exported at the crate root) has passed, its last sleep the time left, then one more settle, while a `render` or `layout` answer returns at once; on `Ok` everything the step made due is on the screen; an instance that does not go quiet is `NotSettled(Busy)`, one still loading at the bound `NotSettled(Loads)`. The step is not rolled back, and no time is advanced — the wait reads `std::time::Instant` and sleeps, with no `tick`, `advance_time` or time step, no changed-set drain, no print and no `tracing` call. - `Refusal` — a `Cause` and, only beside `malformed`, a `Fault`. `CAUSES` is closed at eight (`[Cause; 8]`, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18): `unknown-verb` · `malformed` · `not-found` · `stale` · `disabled` · `covered` · `off-screen` · `fonts-unavailable` (the eighth, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot: meaning "the app this session holds has no font it can paint text with", remedy "boot the app with a font it can decode"), each with a fixed `name()`, `meaning()` and `remedy()`. None of `Cause`, `Fault`, `Refusal` has a `String` field: a refusal holds nothing a call supplied. All eight are returned today — `unknown-verb` and `malformed` by `validate`, the other six by the executor, `fonts-unavailable` from `screenshot`, `lint` and `canvas` among the verbs — a shot checked before anything is painted, a lint, and `Session::lint` in process, before anything is read. On the stand a click is accepted on 68 of the 77 snapshot nodes at boot and refused on 9: the three disabled controls, each task's `task-header-spacer` as `covered` (a box 0 high; the hit at its centre answers the header), and the flight booker's two options `flight-type-one-way` · `flight-type-return` as `covered`, each read at its select's client rect.

- `command_line(args, apps, boot) -> ExitCode` — the whole command line of a binary that boots apps (`boot` an `FnMut` since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface); it installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable. The reader's rules, in order: no first word → usage; `serve <app> --session <dir>` in exactly that shape or with one `--record <dir>` after it, else usage; `mcp` alone or with one `--record <dir>`, else usage (since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface; `--record` since 2026-10-19-session-recording); since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage `coverage <app> <check>...` in that one shape — an app the binary boots, then one or more kept-check paths, no `--session` and no `--record` word among them — else usage, each path read through `File::open(..).take(MAX_CHECK_BYTES + 1)`, then `Check::from_bytes`, a file that cannot be read, one past the bound, one that is no check and a check whose `app()` is not `<app>` refused `malformed`, status `1`, holding nothing of the path or the file, accepted the coverage line on stdout, status `0`, a boot that fails the session error, status `3`, the role calling the binary's boot once per check through `handler_coverage`; a `--record` anywhere else, twice or with no value is usage once the call passed `validate`; `help` with no argument and at most one `--session <dir>`, which is not read, answers `describe()`'s line on stdout, status `0`, reaching no session — `help` with an argument is refused `malformed`, `1`, and `--session` with no directory or given twice is usage, `2` (since 2026-10-12-self-description); a first word the verb table does not hold → the refusal `unknown-verb`; the call the remaining words spell (flags as the schema spells them — `--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--ms` and `--part` each with one value, `--ms`'s and `--part`'s read as a number, `--shift`, `--ctrl` and `--full` bare; `start`'s app as one plain word) is checked by `validate` or `validate_session` before the session address is asked for; then `--session <dir>` exactly once, else usage; `start` on an app the binary does not boot → usage. Four endings: accepted — the answer on stdout, status `0`; refused — the refusal on stdout, `1`; usage — one fixed line on stderr built from `VERBS` and the app names, `2`; session error — the error object on stdout and its message on stderr, `3`; the host role ends quiet, status `0`; the `mcp` role hands stdin and stdout to `serve_mcp` with `IDLE_EXPIRY` and writes nothing on stdout at its end — `0` on `Ok`, `3` with the error's fixed message on stderr on `Err` — and the usage line names it (`; mcp role: mcp [--record <dir>]`, then `; coverage role: coverage <app> <check>...;` before `; apps:`), with `snapshot [--part <part>]`, `graph [--part <part>]` after `lint`, press's `[--ctrl]`, `layout --id <id>` after `actions`, `start <app> [--record <dir>]` and `host role: serve <app> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]`; `start --record` and `mcp --record` check the recording directory first, a refusal ending status `3` with nothing spawned or served. No command's ending writes back anything the caller typed, but `caused` carries an app's own messages and fields as their author wrote them, `error` included, scrubbed by the answer's own hidden field names, so an app that writes typed text into a record echoes it. `start` spawns the running binary again as `serve <app> --session <dir>`, with `--record <dir>` after it when it was given one, its streams closed, waits up to 30 s for it to answer, and neither kills nor reaps it.

- The wire (`wire.rs`, crate-private, versioned `v3`, `v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording) is one request line and one reply line per connection: `hello v3` → `ok v3 pid= label= served= idle_expiry_s=`, `stop v3` → `ok v3 stopping`, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` → `ok v3 accepted <json>` · `ok v3 refused <json>` · `ok v3 oversize` · `ok v3 recording-failed` (sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed`), another version of a known word → `refused version`, anything else → `refused malformed`. - Assert first that the fixture produces the condition under test, then the behaviour; a focus test pins the node focus lands on, never only that a hidden control is not focused (the post-layout focus fixup makes that hold with or without the change under test); a new check is controlled — a named mutation of what it guards turns it red, a case it leaves green widened until it does, and the restored tree reads green; a check never derives its expected value from the constant its mutation control changes, but pins the measured value as a literal (a pixel-row pin that font-embolden moves is pinned as a stated band with its reason in a comment where the test crate cannot see the feature, its wholly-inside assertions kept exact); a control that removes a bound loosens it to twice the budget rather than removing it, so the mutated run stays bounded; a control of a read that must change nothing gives the read pending work that a pass would apply, so a read that ran a pass would be seen (a pump on a settled screen is invisible); a control whose case lies in the later of two test targets named by one gate entry with no fail-fast override needs an edit that leaves the earlier target green (Cargo runs the targets in name order and stops at the first red one, so the named case would go unrun).

The seven served tasks are read on every CI OS by one stand check, `stand_cross_os_readings`, which compares the driver's answer digests for snapshot (every part), lint and actions, at boot and after one acting step in both layout modes, to one committed table, with no shot and no kept check file; a shot of a canvas alone is the one shot compared across OSes, by `stand_canvas_cross_os`: three canvas-alone fixtures (a solid fill, an antialiased edge, canvas glyphs), each shot whole and as its element, and Circle Drawer's canvas shot as its element, in both layout modes, their answer digests held byte-equal on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 to committed tables, no pixels committed, and Circle Drawer's canvas draw commands are read in process by `stand_canvas_commands`, in both layout modes, at boot, after a click and at 12 and 100 circles, as summary, full dump and parts, into one committed table, each answer held equal by size and digest on the same three hosts, while a shot holding document text stays out of every cross-OS byte check; text an app paints on a canvas such a comparison holds (Circle Drawer's diameter label) is drawn with its glyph origins on whole device pixels.
